summary: Everyone wants to be friends with Adil. But how do you start a conversation with someone when their words dance to music you cannot hear? When Adil Speaks, Words Dance is a heart-warming tale of empathy, inclusivity and the surprising superpowers of friendship.

title: When God Made the World
author: Matthew Paul Turner
summary: From the author of the bestselling children's book When God Made You comes a rhythmic, whimsical journey through creation--for little readers who love science and wonder and the beginnings of all things.

title: When I was Four
author: Chef Rosetta M. Stevenson
summary: When I Was Four tells the true story of Zetta Marie, who is deaf, and a chef, a deaf chef! When Zetta was four she opened a can of frozen grape juice concentrate and added three cans of water. She was hooked! She also watched her mama cooking in the kitchen and was inspired to start writing her own recipes, secretly slipping them into her mama’s recipe book. While spending time baking pies with her Grammie and playing with the dough, she started pretending she was a chef, owned a restaurant and had bake sales. The dreams of her future began. Filled with cute and colorful illustrations, follow Zetta on her discovery of her love for baking and making her dreams come true. Today Zetta is a professional pastry chef and has a degree in Culinary Art, Professional Baking and Pastry and Hospitality Management. She wants all children to know that your disability shouldn’t stop you from daydreaming about your future and if you stay focused you can be and do anything, just like she did!

title: When I Wear My Crown
author: Jeanna Ganas & Shayla Jackson
summary: Shayla, Miss GA Teen USA 2020 was diagnosed with hearing loss when she was 3 years old. This news was life changing, however she never let her hearing impairment dictate what she was capable of achieving. This book shows that all children with a disability has a hidden crown inside them.

title: Where are my Hearing Aids?
author: Paula Villaboim Farrugia
summary: "Oh no, oh dear! My hearing aids are lost!" Follow along on a delightful adventure in the search for missing hearing aids - from the bedroom to the kitchen, and to the bath to the yard. Will she find her hearing aids? Where Are My Hearing Aids? supports language development and early literacy skills through playful rhymes and engaging repetition, making it ideal for children aged 0 and up. Every child who wears hearing aids understands the feeling of losing them. The hunt for the missing hearing aids becomes more than just a search—it's an adventure that mirrors the real emotions and challenges faced by young children with hearing loss, offering them comfort in knowing they are not alone in this experience.

title: Where I Stand: On the Signing Community and My DeafBlind Experience
author: John Lee Clark
summary: This collection of essays from one of the country's leading voices on issues facing the signing community appears at a time of troubling trends and exciting new developments. Through his lucid and accessible prose, John Lee Clark delves into questions ranging from why hearing parents of Deaf children don't sign to how written American Sign Language will change the course of Deaf literature. As a second-generation DeafBlind man, Clark also takes us on a tour of his experiences as a student, father, husband, and "client" of special services. Filled with startling observations and unapologetic assertions, Where I Stand challenges and broadens readers' understanding of an important but often overlooked community.

title: Where is the Bird?
author: Victoria Forrest
summary: An augmented reality (AR) children's book by Victoria Forrest (VIKA Books) designed to teach British Sign Language (BSL) to families. It uses smartphone technology to bring illustrations to life, focusing on early communication and interaction between babies and adults

title: Where Would the World Be Without Charlie
author: Lauren Freeman
summary: A children's book that  follows a charming boy named Charlie, who wears hearing aids, on a journey of self-discovery at the zoo. The story focuses on embracing differences as unique, rather than limiting.

title: Whisper
author: Chrissie Keighery
summary: I'm always trying to figure out what's really going on. Always having to fill in the gaps, but never getting all the details. It's like trying to do a jigsaw when I don't even know what the picture is, and I'm missing one of the vital middle pieces. How do you know if your friends are talking about you being your back, or if a boy likes you? They could act all innocent, but you'd know from the rumors. You'd hear the whispers. But what if you couldn't hear those whispers anymore? Being a teenager is hard enough. But what about being a deaf teenager? Demi is 15 years old when her world is shattered by illness. Waking up in hospital, she can see people are talking and moving around her, but she can hear nothing. As the days and weeks pass, it becomes clear that Demi is locked in a silent world and this is a world she must now learn to navigate. This unique, touching story explores the universal theme of finding your place, against a fascinating backdrop.

title: Whispers and Echoes: Stories of Hearing Loss for Kids
author: Erin L. Stilwell
summary: Whispers and Echoes: Stories of Hearing Loss for Kids is a touching collection of short stories that invites young readers into the diverse and heartfelt experiences of children who navigate the world with hearing loss. With warmth, sensitivity, and imagination, each story reveals how sound can be felt, seen, or sensed in unique and meaningful ways. Whether it’s the soft rhythm of a parent’s heartbeat, the discovery of a new hearing device, or the courage to stand tall in a noisy world, the characters in these pages reflect real challenges and real triumphs. Along the way, readers will encounter themes of resilience, friendship, creativity, and belonging. Perfect for children with hearing loss, their families, classmates, and educators, this book gently fosters empathy and inclusion—encouraging all readers to appreciate the many ways we listen, communicate, and connect. Whispers and Echoes is more than just a book—it’s a celebration of hearing differences, a tribute to every child’s inner strength, and a powerful reminder that our stories—whispered or echoed—deserve to be heard.

title: Why I Need My Hearing Aids
author: Sofia Ali
summary: Written from the perspective of a young girl, this picture book shows how a resilient little girl comes to terms with her need for hearing aids and her resilience. This book will go a long way into communicating the experiences to other children who wear hearing aids.

title: Wild
author: Hannah Moskowitz
summary: Zack Ramos is training for two things: being a parent to his twelve-year-old sister once his mother's early-onset Alzheimer's (the same kind he and his sister each have a 50% chance of developing--but let's not think about that) progresses too far, and running a one hundred mile race through the mountains of Tennessee. His support system is longtime girlfriend Jordan Jonas, who's sweet, sarcastic, and entirely virtual. They've been talking for years but still have never met in person. Because Jordan, it turns out, was still waiting for the right time to tell him that she's Deaf. The revelation brings them closer together, and Zack throws himself into learning sign language and trying to navigate their way through their different cultures. But with the stress of a tumultuous relationship, a new language, a sick mother, and his uncertain future, there's going to be a breaking point...and it might be out there in the Tennessee wild.

title: Will Wonder and His Robot Ears
author: Med-El
summary: MED-EL’s comic book series is designed to appeal to a young audience by introducing the topic of hearing implants in a fun way. Introduced in July 2011, the comic book features the young superhero, Will Wonder, and his bilateral cochlear implants. Will’s “Robot Ears” help him to hear and communicate with others, and his newly-discovered special powers make him more sensitive to the vibrations given off by other people, the earth and the environment.

title: Will Wonder and the Chain of Three
author: Med-El
summary: MED-EL’s comic book series is designed to appeal to a young audience by introducing the topic of hearing implants in a fun way. Introduced in July 2011, the comic book features the young superhero, Will Wonder, and his bilateral cochlear implants. Will’s “Robot Ears” help him to hear and communicate with others, and his newly-discovered special powers make him more sensitive to the vibrations given off by other people, the earth and the environment.

title: Wind
author: Child's Play
summary: Let's play out in the wind! There's a wealth of sights, sounds, smells, tastes and textures to discover and enjoy! In this series of richly illustrated books, Carol Thompson celebrates the immediate and sensory response of children to the natural world - whatever the weather!

title: Winnie's ASL Adventure: Left
author: Deb Myers
summary: Gramma takes Winnie on a surprise trip, and what begins as a simple walk becomes a heartwarming adventure full of discovery, connection, and joy. Along the way, readers enjoy vibrant illustrations, playful storytelling, and a closer look at the many ways to sign LEFT in American Sign Language. This beautifully illustrated book, the second in this series, reminds us that surprises come in all shapes, sizes, and meanings.

title: Winnie's ASL Adventure: Wash
author: Deb Myers
summary: Go on an adventure with Winnie and her gramma as they WASH all day long! The first in a series, this full-color book will delight children and adults alike as they discover that a word can have multiple signs and meanings. Each page is beautifully illustrated, incorporating cultural and linguistic aspects. At the end of the book are illustrations demonstrating the many ways to sign WASH for different contexts. WASH is the first book in the Winnie's ASL Adventures series.

title: Winning Sounds Like This: A Season with the Women's Basketball Team at Gallaudet, the World's Only Deaf University
author: Wayne R. Coffey
summary: Winning Sounds Like This: A Season with the Women's Basketball Team at Gallaudet, the World's Only Deaf University (2002) is a non-fiction book by Wayne R. Coffey chronicling the 1999-2000 season of the Gallaudet University women's basketball team. It details the team's pursuit of an NCAA Division III championship under coach Kitty Baldridge, focusing on Deaf culture, communication challenges, and the players' lives.

title: Wired for Sound: A Journey into Hearing
author: Beverly Biderman
summary: The author recounts her experiences with progressive hereditary hearing loss and the changes in her life after receiving a cochlear implant, an artificial sensory organ.

title: Wonder
author: R.J. Palacio
summary: August Pullman is not an ordinary ten-year-old kid. Sure, he's a huge Star Wars fan, he loves his dog, and he's got a pretty good sense of humor. But August was born with a craniofacial abnormality, a genetic defect that caused his facial features to be severely deformed. His life has never been "normal." Despite his differences, August and his parents decide to transition him from home school to private school now that he's entering fifth grade. It's the start of middle school, they reason, so everyone will be new. But August has to deal with so much more than just being new. Will he make friends? Will he decide to stay at the school? And can the people around him learn to see past his appearance? This brilliant, sensitive story, narrated not only by August, but also by his older sister, his classmates, and other kids in his life, takes an insightful look at how one person's differences can affect the lives of so many others.

title: Wonderful Me: A First Guide to Taking Care of Yourself
author: Nancy Shapiro
summary: Discover simple ways children can look after themselves, from naming feelings and moving their body, to building boundaries, and caring for their friends! Learning to look after yourself is an important part of growing up, and it can also be fun! By being mindful of their mental, physical, and social wellbeing, children can be more confident in navigating tricky situations and new experiences. Whether it is taking care of their senses, learning about respect, or unwinding when they feel overwhelmed, this book is packed full of helpful ideas and tips for little ones and their grown-ups. Written by clinical psychologist and author, Nancy Shapiro, who believes that teaching children how to care for themselves can help them in later life, this book’s impactful information is balanced out by cute and bright illustrations from Vânia Sacramento.

title: Wonderful Woods
author: Laura Blum
summary: Wonderful Woods Rhymes When Signed Baby Board Book is simple to sign for families learning ASL. Each book pairs an animal with either a color or number that shares the same handshapes. Parents and children love signing these simple rhymes while learning their colors and numbers 1-5. Illustrated by Deaf Artist Larry Laskowski and children young and old love his enchanting watercolor creatures. Be sure to scan the QR code on the back of each book to learn the signs and see how they rhyme! The intention behind our books and resources are to promote parent - child bonding and language through shared reading and interactions through play. This book is written in English to be simple to sign!

title: Wonderfully Different, Wonderfully Me
author: Becky Zingale
summary: Wonderfully Different, Wonderfully Me is the first book written by Becky Zingale. Becky’s husband, Duane, and their younger daughter have the same syndrome as the main character in the book and movie Wonder. Becky wanted to a similar book for a younger audience. She looked for children’s books with pictures of children who have facial differences and wear Bone Anchored Hearing Aids. Unable to find any such books, Becky’s husband Duane, encouraged her to create the solution, by writing children’s books to share the stories of their family and friends. Becky wanted not only her own daughter, but all children, to see themselves in Wonderfully Different, Wonderfully Me whether they connect with a character’s personal challenges, physical appearance, or personality.

title: Wonderstruck
author: Brian Selznick
summary: Wonderstruck by Brian Selznick is a young adult novel that interweaves two parallel stories, one in words and pictures, the other in pictures alone, about two deaf children—Ben in 1977 and Rose in 1927—who journey to New York City seeking family and belonging, with their narratives eventually connecting through their shared experiences and a mysterious actress. The book explores themes of silence, collection, and the quest for connection, and was adapted into a film by Todd Haynes.

title: World of Silence
author: Kaytlin Phillips
summary: Fledge Owenby was born deaf and has spent his whole life trying to prove himself, but even becoming an exceptional archer and devising a plan to fight in the war, despite his deafness, isn’t enough. Stuck in the bunker he calls home with the women, Fledge is anything but pleased as his brothers and friend leave to help vanquish the dragons. When the unexpected happens, leaving Fledge alone in the bunker with dangers abounding outside he must find a way to survive. A way to prove to everyone that just because he can’t hear, doesn’t mean he’s useless. Saved from danger by a dragoness, Fledge wonders why she—his supposed enemy—would help him? Drawn together by a bond, not even he can understand, Fledge and Galexia are unwittingly pulled into adventure. Betrayal of the highest level, deception unparalleled, and a war that never should have been. Fledge must find a way to end it all and prove his own worth at the same time.

title: Worries: A lift-the-flap board book
author: Pat-a-Cake
summary: Find Out About: Worries helps curious preschoolers through common anxieties – like separation anxiety and fear of the dark – an encourages mindful thinking and empathetic behaviour. Featuring friendly child characters and familiar situations, they will find answers and reassurance when they are feeling worried. With fun flaps to lift and a memory game at the end, this is an excellent book for children and parents to share together.

title: You and Me
author: Child's Play
summary: A new baby needs looking after all the time! It's the perfect opportunity for older siblings to enjoy how much more grown-up and independent they are. A new addition to any family is exciting, but the experience can also be worrying and confusing for siblings. Coping with the new situations and emotions that arise can be very challenging. This series of four board books deals with the anticipation of waiting for the new baby, the excitement of the arrival itself, and the beginnings of the special relationship that develops between siblings. The simple conversational text and lively illustrations are carefully designed to encourage further dialogue between reader and child.

title: You are Enough
author: Margaret O'Hair
summary: You Are Enough: A Book About Inclusion is a children's picture book by Margaret O'Hair, inspired by Sofia Sanchez, a model and actress with Down syndrome, celebrating self-acceptance and diversity through colorful illustrations and a message that everyone belongs and is enough just as they are. The book encourages children to embrace their differences, be confident, and promotes inclusion, featuring a diverse cast of characters and including back matter with information about Down syndrome and acceptance.

title: You Can!: Kids Empowering Kids
author: Alexandra Strick
summary: You can . . . be brave, challenge yourself, overcome your fears, be kind, be YOU! Come on an amazing journey with fourteen young people as they grow from birth to eighteen, learning new skills, exploring new worlds, standing up for their own and others’ rights, and following their dreams. Created in consultation with real young adults, Alexandra Strick’s groundbreaking narrative will inspire and empower young people of all ages and abilities to believe in themselves and follow their own path, especially during tough times. Complemented by Steve Antony’s exuberant and inclusive artwork, which introduces fourteen comparable fictional characters and tracks their growth page by page, You Can! is a timely and meaningful gift for graduates or any reader marking significant milestones.

title: You Don't Know Everything Jilly P!
author: Alex Gino
summary: You Don't Know Everything, Jilly P! by Alex Gino is a middle-grade novel about a white, hearing girl who learns about disability, race, and privilege after her baby sister is born deaf. Jilly, a fantasy fan, connects with a Black, Deaf boy online for help, leading her to confront her own biases and understand the world's different experiences, including racism and police violence, through her sister, her cousins, and her new friend. The book explores themes of allyship, family, and the importance of being open to change and learning.

title: You Should Be Grateful
author: Angela Tucker
summary: “Your parents are so amazing for adopting you! You should be grateful that you were adopted.” Angela Tucker is a Black woman, adopted from foster care by white parents. She has heard this microaggression her entire life, usually from well-intentioned strangers who view her adoptive parents as noble saviors. She is grateful for many aspects of her life, but being transracially adopted involves layers of rejection, loss, and complexity that cannot be summed up so easily. In “You Should Be Grateful,” Tucker centers the experiences of adoptees to share deeply personal stories, well-researched history, and engrossing anecdotes from mentorship sessions with adopted youth. These perspectives challenge the fairy-tale narrative of adoption, giving way to a fuller story that explores the impacts of racism, classism, family, love, and belonging.

title: You'll Always Have a Friend
author: Emily Ley
summary: You'll Always Have a Friend: What to Do When the Lonelies Come by Emily Ley is a 2024 children's book that helps kids navigate feelings of loneliness by offering practical tools and reassurance, encouraging them to be brave, kind, and inclusive to build friendships, and reminding them that everyone feels lonely sometimes. Illustrated by Romina Galotta, the book provides gentle, positive strategies for making friends and coping with being left out, making it a great read for back-to-school anxiety.

title: You're Welcome Universe!
author: Whitney Gardner
summary: When Julia finds a slur about her best friend scrawled across the back of the Kingston School for the Deaf, she covers it up with a beautiful (albeit illegal) graffiti mural. Her supposed best friend snitches, the principal expels her, and her two mothers set Julia up with a one-way ticket to a “mainstream” school in the suburbs, where she’s treated like an outcast as the only deaf student. The last thing she has left is her art, and not even Banksy himself could convince her to give that up. Out in the ’burbs, Julia paints anywhere she can, eager to claim some turf of her own. But Julia soon learns that she might not be the only vandal in town. Someone is adding to her tags, making them better, showing off—and showing Julia up in the process. She expected her art might get painted over by cops. But she never imagined getting dragged into a full-blown graffiti war. Told with wit and grit by debut author Whitney Gardner, who also provides gorgeous interior illustrations of Julia’s graffiti tags, You’re Welcome, Universe introduces audiences to a one-of-a-kind protagonist who is unabashedly herself no matter what life throws in her way.

title: Young Thomas Edison
author: Michael Dooling
summary: Young Thomas Edison by Michael Dooling is a children's picture book biography that explores the early life of the famous inventor, focusing on his childhood curiosity, early experiments (sometimes explosive), struggles in school, and entrepreneurial spirit as a paperboy and newspaper publisher. The book highlights how his mother's support and his own determination laid the groundwork for his future success, using clear text and detailed illustrations to tell the story of his formative year.

title: Zola Gets Hearing Aids
author: Narita Snead
summary: Zola has a problem. She does not hear as well as other kids. Today is the day she goes to the doctor, a special doctor, to check her hearing. Zola is worried because she has heard all about those kids who do not hear well. Her greatest fear is having to wear a hearing aid. She is worried about how her friends will react if she has to get a hearing aid and wear it to school. Will they tease her? Will she be bullied or will they accept her and still be her friend? Not sure about what the day will bring, with great sadness and frustration, she pushes back her blanket and gets out of the bed to go to the doctor’s office.

title: Zola's Teachable Moment
author: Narita Snead
summary: Zola has great news! Her teacher has given the class a very important project. Zola is excited because the project will allow her to teach the class something. She is also very nervous because she has never taught a class before. What will she teach everyone that will make a difference? That night in her sleep, Zola is visited by someone who takes her on a journey to help her decide what she can teach about. Find out who Zola meets and how she discovers her teachable moment.

title: Zoom, Zoom, Zoom!
author: Child's Play
summary: This charming series has been specifically designed for babies. A great introduction to books through well—known nursery rhymes and interactive text. Singing songs and rhymes is the perfect way to bond with your baby and share quality time. It also aids language development by introducing them to the natural sounds and patterns of speech. Combining these with actions also stimulates the brain and helps muscle development.
